title: does latency matter as much in ai trading?
author: Annual-Register-3683
selftext:
I've been messing around with AI lately to help me look at charts and sort through trade ideas. It started as a side project, but now I'm wondering if it could actually do more.

That made me think about latency. If AI is helping with entries or even placing trades, how much does execution speed really matter? Is it mostly a scalping thing, or does it still matter for other styles too?

comments.author: VexorLabs
comments.body:
AI can help with analysis, but AI alone won’t make a trading system profitable. You still need market knowledge, execution infrastructure, risk filters, liquidity checks and speed.

Latency matters a lot for strategies like sniping, MEV, arbitrage and fast entries. If the signal is good but execution is slow, the opportunity can be gone before the trade lands.

That’s why Vexor is built as a full AI DeFi trading platform, not just a chatbot reading charts. It combines AI scanning, token risk analysis, sniping, MEV, arbitrage and automated execution in one system.

https://vexorbot.com/

comments.author: mdawe1
comments.body: Depends on the length of your holds. It also adds another cost along side commission and spread losses that eat marginal gains. You will find out that most LLM’s are very risk adverse by design and need a ton of prompt engineering to not give them an easy out solution. I never really found anything better then a coin flip with them
